headline: Large User Grid Cost Responsibility
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the financial burden of grid infrastructure costs from residential ratepayers to large energy users, primarily data centers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: Virginia requires data centers to pay for their own power lines
news_summary: Virginia's State Corporation Commission decided that data centers must pay the full cost for the transmission infrastructure projects they require, preventing these costs from falling on residential ratepayers. This decision aligns with Governor Spanberger's call to shift the burden to large energy users, potentially saving Virginia residents hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Data Center Water Use Disclosure
short_summary: This legislation mandates that data centers report their water consumption, providing transparency on their environmental footprint and aiding state regulators in water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Virginia DEQ.
opponents: Data center industry (potentially due to reporting burden/scrutiny).
news_headline: Virginia study on groundwater, data centers calls for tighter water regulations
news_summary: A long-delayed Virginia study found declining groundwater availability in the eastern coastal plain due to population and industrial use, urging stricter regulations on water withdrawal permits. The report noted limits on publicly available data center water use information, which SB 553 aims to address by requiring reporting.

headline: Data Center Local Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill grants local governments more control over where data centers can be built and imposes requirements for site assessments examining noise and other potential impacts on nearby communities.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, local planning and public health organizations.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry (potentially due to increased regulatory hurdles).
news_headline: Virginia tightens data center restrictions amid political backlash
news_summary: Virginia is implementing stricter permitting, commercial, and environmental controls on data centers due to growing political backlash. Governor Spanberger's "Data Center Accountability Framework" includes expediting new state noise regulations and strengthening local control over siting.
